graduation_requirements.raw_text:
MAUHS students take a minimum of 24 required and elective courses to meet content learning
expectations reported through domains linked to proficiency-based graduation requirements.
Beginning with the Class of 2024 students must meet graduation requirements in alignment with
Vermont Educational Quality Standards. This shift is required by Vermont Act 77 and reflects best
practices for students to be prepared for college, careers, and community in our ever-changing
world. Instead of a set number of credits and courses, MAUHS students will need to demonstrate
they have achieved proficiency in:
Required Credits in Subject Areas:
• English 4 credits
• Global Citizenship 3 credits
• Math 3 credits
• Science (1 Life, 1 Physical) 3 credits
• Physical Education 1.5 credits
• Health .5 credit

• Art 1 credit
• Technology .5 credit
• Other electives 6.5 credits
• Class of 2029: Civics / Financial Literacy 1 credit
• Class of 2020: Completion of Personalized
Learning Plan (4 years)

______________________________________________________________________________

Graduation Requirements
MAUHS requires 24 credits for graduation. Course requirements for graduation meet local and state standards.
Some Southwest Tech Programs have embedded graduation requirement credit(s). See the SWT Program of
Studies and check with your school counselor about such courses. Students may not be promoted to the next grade
level unless they have earned a minimum of credits (below) by August 1st of each school year. 9th and 10th graders
will remain in that grade for the entire year regardless of credits earned midyear. 11th graders can be promoted
to 12th grade at the end of the 1st semester if they have earned 18 credits and have the potential to earn 24 credits
by June of that school year to graduate.

courses.description: Students will learn professional quality software used to retouch photos, color and manipulate images. Students begin with a tutorial to learn the software tools and then apply these skills to solve visual design problems. This course can be used to complete an Art or Tech credit.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement; This course can be used to complete an Art or Tech credit.

courses.description: A studio workshop where students explore basic design principles. Instruction will focus on increasing the student's powers of observation and his/her ability to draw and create. Included will be identification of basic forms, an understanding of space, shading to create realistic drawings, and fundamentals of two-dimensional design. Students will work mostly in pencil, charcoal and pastel. Some color will be discussed. There will also be discussion of artists and their works through images, videos, and prints. Sketchbook is required.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: During this course, basic drawing and design skills are developed and increased in range through a variety of advanced techniques and media. This course will include: color theory, color mixing, paint application and collage. Students will work in a range of paint media, including watercolor and acrylic. Some basic art appreciation and history is included. Sketchbook required. Prerequisite: Art 1
courses.prerequisites: Art 1
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: Students will explore drawing and painting at a more advanced level-allowing room for self expression and giving choice of materials when possible. The awareness that art expresses human ideas and feelings should encourage students to explore directions of self-expression. Materials will include (but not be limited to) pencil, pen, acrylic, watercolor, pastels and 3D. Prerequisite: Art 1 & 2
courses.prerequisites: Art 1 & 2
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: Students will consult with the art instructor to determine a program and materials. The instructor will provide direction and supervision. However, students must be able to work independently. Periodic conferences with the instructor are held for students to present work completed. Prerequisite: Art 3 and teacher approval.
courses.prerequisites: Art 3 and teacher approval.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: Introduction to working with clay. The course will emphasize the three basic hand-building methods: pinch, coil and slab. These methods will be used to create objects, both functional and sculptural, of the student's own design. In addition, students will be introduced to wheel throwing. A sketchbook is required.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: Students will focus on wheel throwing combined with ceramics one hand building techniques. Students will further develop craftsmanship techniques. A sketchbook is required. Prerequisite: Ceramics 1.
courses.prerequisites: Ceramics 1.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: This advanced ceramics course is partially developed by the student in consultation with the teacher. There will be an emphasis placed on craftsmanship and rate of production. Students will learn to load and fire kilns. Students must be able to work independently. Sketchbook is required. Prerequisite: Ceramics 2 and teacher approval.
courses.prerequisites: Ceramics 2 and teacher approval.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: Students will consult with the instructor to determine a program. The instructor will provide direction and supervision. Students must be able to work independently in the areas of ceramics or sculpture. Periodic conferences with the instructor are held for students to present work completed and could include developing a portfolio. A sketchbook is required. Prerequisite: Ceramics 3 and teacher approval.
courses.prerequisites: Ceramics 3 and teacher approval.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: Students will explore a variety of printmaking techniques, including carving, etching, multi-media and experimental printmaking, mono printing, and solar/photographic prints. We will explore additive and reductive processes. We will also explore computer assisted image making and we will examine the work of traditional and contemporary print makers. Students will learn the elements and principals of design as a foundation for creating works of art. Recommendations: Due to the sharp and potentially harmful nature of the tools used, students must be mature and trustworthy.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: This course offers students the chance to be creative in the historical art forms of quilting, and sewing. Hand Sewing and machine sewing will be explored through various projects. Other crafts including knitting, crocheting, needlepoint, stenciling, stamping, etc. will be introduced. Students who have not taken the course in the past will have priority for admission. If space is available a student may, with teacher permission, take the course a second time.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement
courses.notes: Also listed under Electives (SB Quilting is a separate short-block course)

courses.description: This courses is a hands-on studio course for students who like to try a little bit of everything. Screen print your own t-shirt! Try calligraphy! Design and construct your own sketchbook! Make a miniature keychain book! Design and print on paper and fabric. You will even work with clay! Students will explore a variety of hands-on art materials and methods for art making. We will take our inspiration from social media and you! Tell us what you’d like to try.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: An introduction to the use of the camera, film exposure and basic dark room skills. This includes film and print development, editing, mixing, storing and using chemicals, and presentation skills. The course will also cover a brief history of black and white photography. Due to potentially harmful nature of chemistry and darkroom use, students must be trustworthy and mature. An application must be completed and reviewed with teacher approval to take the course. 35 mm camera is required as well. Prerequisite: Art 1 or teacher approval with application completed.
courses.prerequisites: Art 1 or teacher approval with application completed.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses listed in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: This course is a performing ensemble with a minimum of four mandatory performances per year. Concert music is selected from various historical time periods including Renaissance, Classical, Romantic, Contemporary, and Pop. Development of proper vocal techniques, with a focus on basic music elements are explored. Included with vocal and musical development are mandatory rotating group vocal lessons. Qualified students are eligible to audition for Vermont Green Mountain Music District, All-State and New England Music Festivals. Concert performances for these prestigious opportunities are held in March and May. Each spring semester the Music Department ensembles travel to music competitions and festivals; fund-raising is necessary. Grades are based on class, lessons and performance attendance. There are written exams in January and June.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: Students will learn how to record music digitally and will demonstrate proficiency with the instruments and audio equipment used in popular music and digital audio production. Students will also examine popular music history beginning in the 1950s to the present, examining different genres, style periods, and artists with historical context. Student learning will be assessed using project-based authentic performance tasks, in addition to content-driven formal summative assessments.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: This is a performance based class. Students are required to perform at home football games, town parades, concerts, band camp, graduation, and on awards nights. Students are issued a uniform and some instruments are available. The band travels occasionally to perform in music festivals throughout the district, state and New England. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor or a previous year in school band program.
courses.prerequisites: Consent of instructor or a previous year in school band program.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: This course explores the elements of music and how they are put together. The focus is songwriting. Students create their own songs while learning to read and write music. Students planning to major in music in college will need to have this course. Students will use computers, Sibelius2 music program and be a part of the Vermont Midi Project.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: This course is intended for the student desiring to learn the basics of both the guitar and the keyboard. It provides an introduction to standard music notation and music terminology as it relates to both instruments. Students learn to play single note melodies and a variety of accompaniment patterns. Students will enjoy playing a variety of songs in a variety of styles. Grades are based on preparation, practice, class participation and weekly in-class performances. There are written and playing mid-term and final exams. The semester would be divided into 4 units: 1.) Intro. to music reading and basics of both instruments; 2.) Students choose keyboard or guitar to focus on for 4 weeks; 3.) Students switch to the other instrument for 4 weeks; and, 4.) Students select which instrument to continue to work on for the rest of the semester to become more proficient.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses in this section meet the MAUHS Art requirement

courses.description: This course examines various pieces of literature, historical figures, and film, students will be looking at “The Hero’s Journey” in order to determine, “What is a Hero? How does the Journey shape the Hero? This course differs from the A-level in that students complete reading and writing more independently and at a faster pace. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and MS student performance.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and MS student performance.
courses.notes: Heading in catalog: English 9 Honors Humanities (& 460 SS 1 World Honors Humanities)

courses.description: Through various literary and historical text and film, students will be looking at “The Hero’s Journey” in order to determine, “What is a Hero? How does the Journey shape the Hero?” Students will strengthen critical reading, writing, and vocabulary skills.
courses.notes: Heading in catalog: English 9A Humanities (& 461 SS1 World Academic Humanities)

courses.description: This course focuses on building strong basic reading and writing skills. Students will learn about basic sentence structure, grammar, and vocabulary. Students will write short to mid-length pieces and read a range of literature, focusing on character development and exploring the essential question "What Makes a Hero?"
courses.notes: Applied level; Heading in catalog: English 9 Applied Humanities (& 462 SS1 World Applied Humanities)

courses.description: This course emphasizes literary analysis and begins with an examination of text for rhetorical strategies including diction, imagery, sentence structure, syntax, language and details. Readings include literature from Africa, Asia and the classics to examine the essential question: how does the human spirit cope with challenges? Students will be expected to complete summer reading texts and assigned work related to these texts that are due the 1st day of school. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 English.

courses.description: How do people cope with challenges? Through exploring world literature, students will analyze diverse cultural values/beliefs and how individuals cope with challenges they face. Students will broaden their own perspectives and roles as global citizens. What characteristics embody strength in facing adversity? Students will strengthen critical reading, writing, and vocabulary skills. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 English.

courses.description: What do people do when their very survival is at stake? How do they overcome challenges that are internal and/or external in the midst of survival situations? This course explores these questions through reading both fiction and nonfiction texts in a strategic learning environment. Students will learn strategies to build reading fluency, comprehension, vocabulary, and writing skills. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 English.
courses.notes: Applied level

courses.description: In this course, students read and analyze prose written in a variety of periods, disciplines and rhetorical contexts; emphasis is on American literature, but additional works are included. This course develops skills in argumentation, rhetoric, persuasion, and style analysis. It is expected that each student takes the AP exam in May. Students are expected to complete summer reading assignments. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 & 10 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 & 10 English.

courses.description: In this course students survey American literature while analyzing language and developing their ability to use language effectively in their own writing. The primary focus in this advanced level course is analysis through close readings of seminal works of American literature and other texts that examine the American Dream and the struggles people encounter as they define their identity and discover who they are while trying to fulfill their American Dream. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 & 10 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 & 10 English.

courses.description: Through exploration of diverse American texts, students will identify and analyze the struggles people encounter while pursuing their hopes and dreams. Students will broaden their own perspectives and roles as American citizens. What tensions arise when the demands of society and the individual’s desire for self-development clash? What incongruity exists between the reality and the promise of the American dream? Students will strengthen critical reading, writing, and vocabulary skills. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 & 10 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 & 10 English.

courses.description: This course focuses on improving essential reading and writing skills required for college and career readiness. Readings on the theme of Hopes and Dreams will focus on increased comprehension plot, character, motivation, and theme. Analysis practice will be used to dive deeper into texts through writing. Writing strategies, vocabulary and grammar study will scaffold deeper analysis and writing skills. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 & 10 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 & 10 English.
courses.notes: Applied level

courses.description: This course focuses on British literature and emphasizes the writing of college level critical/analytical papers with in class impromptu pieces and longer polished papers. Students taking this course are expected to take the AP exam in May and enroll in the short block review section second semester. This course builds upon the skills students developed in AP English 11 and adds poetry analysis and interpretation. Students are expected to complete summer reading assignments. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9, 10, & 11 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9, 10, & 11 English.

courses.description: How does literature address humanity’s ability--or inability--to face the pressures of the society in which it lives? Who holds the power in society? Do the alienated and outcast challenge or maintain the values and beliefs of their society? What do you learn about yourself and others when reading works of fiction and nonfiction? Complex and diverse texts both classic and modern will be analyzed. Students will strengthen skills in reading, writing, and thinking. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9, 10, & 11 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9, 10, & 11 English.

courses.description: Through exploration of complex and diverse texts both classic and modern, including selections from British Literature, students will analyze the theme of The Individual Society. Do the alienated and outcast challenge or maintain the values and beliefs of their society? What do you learn about yourself and others when reading works of fiction and nonfiction? Students will strengthen skills in reading, writing, and thinking. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9, 10, & 11 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9, 10, & 11 English.

courses.description: This course focuses on improving reading and writing skills required for college and career readiness by focusing on works related to the theme of The Individual in Society. Close reading works on bolstering comprehension and analysis. Strategic writing instruction progresses through all the constructs of writing from sentences to paragraphs to essays, and provides patterns to use for improving in all areas of writing. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9, 10, & 11 English.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9, 10, & 11 English.
courses.notes: Applied level

courses.description: This course introduces basic language structures, skills & vocabulary to students on an intense level. Students will develop the fundamentals of the four language skills: reading, writing, listening, & speaking, as well as a basic understanding of the culture of German speaking countries. Prerequisite: Simultaneous enrollment in B level or higher in English or teacher approval.
courses.prerequisites: Simultaneous enrollment in B level or higher in English or teacher approval.

courses.description: This course is sequential to German 1. While reinforcing skills previously learned, students will continue to increase their knowledge of vocabulary, grammatical structures and German-speaking cultures. The focus is to improve proficiency in the language in the areas of listening, speaking, reading, and writing, using present, past and future tenses and vocabulary acquired in both German 1 and 2. Prerequisite: German 1 with a passing grade.
courses.prerequisites: German 1 with a passing grade.

courses.description: This I sequential to German 2. Previously learned skills continue to be reinforced, while language structures of increasing complexity are presented. The focus is on use of additional tenses such a future, conditional and compound tenses. There’s more opportunity to practice and improve all four language skills as students increase language proficiency. Prerequisite: German 2 with a passing grade.
courses.prerequisites: German 2 with a passing grade.

courses.description: This I sequential to German 3. Previously learned skills continue to be reinforced, while language structures of increasing complexity are presented. There’s more opportunity to practice and improve all four language skills as students increase language proficiency. Prerequisite: German 3 with a passing grade.
courses.prerequisites: German 3 with a passing grade.

courses.description: This AP German Language and Culture course emphasizes communication (understanding and being understood by others) by applying interpersonal, interpretive, and presentational skills in real-life situations. This includes vocabulary usage, language control, communication strategies, and cultural awareness. The AP German Language and Culture course strives not to overemphasize grammatical accuracy at the expense of communication. To best facilitate the study of language and culture, the course is taught almost exclusively in German. The AP German Language and Culture course engages students in an exploration of culture in both contemporary and historical contexts. The course develops students’ awareness and appreciation of cultural products (e.g., tools, books, music, laws, conventions, institutions); practices (patterns of social interactions within a culture); and perspectives (values, attitudes, and assumptions). Prerequisites: German 4
courses.prerequisites: German 4

courses.description: This is the first course of a four-course sequence of Spanish. This course introduces basic language structures, skills and vocabulary to students. Students will develop the four language skills (reading, writing, listening, and speaking) as well as an understanding of Hispanic culture. Prerequisite: Simultaneous enrollment in B level or higher English and Math courses or approval by administration.
courses.prerequisites: Simultaneous enrollment in B level or higher English and Math courses or approval by administration.

courses.description: This course is sequential to Spanish 1. While reinforcing skills previously learned, students will continue to increase their knowledge of vocabulary, grammatical structures and Hispanic culture. The focus is to improve proficiency in the language in the areas of listening, speaking, reading, and writing, using present and past tenses and vocabulary acquired in both Spanish 1 and 2. Prerequisite: Spanish 1 with a grade of at least a 75% or teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Spanish 1 with a grade of at least a 75% or teacher recommendation.

courses.description: This is sequential to Spanish 2. Previously learned skills continue to be reinforced, while language structures of increasing complexity are presented. The focus is on use of additional tenses such as future, conditional and compound tenses. There’s more opportunity to practice and improve all four language skills as students increase language proficiency. Prerequisite: Spanish 2 with a grade of at least a 75% or teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Spanish 2 with a grade of at least a 75% or teacher recommendation.

courses.description: In this course, students continue with the study of grammar, focusing on present subjunctive, and imperative forms. The class is conducted almost entirely in the target language with the goal of improving oral and written proficiency. In order to broaden their understanding of Hispanic cultures, students will do an extensive study of Hispanic art or history and are expected to read literary works of various genres. Preparation for the SAT Subject Test and AP tests begins in this course. Prerequisite: Spanish 3 with a grade of at least a 75% or teacher recommendation
courses.prerequisites: Spanish 3 with a grade of at least a 75% or teacher recommendation

courses.description: In this course, students continue to increase their knowledge of vocabulary and grammar while practicing and refining their communication skills in the target language. The curriculum is based on the 6 themes that correspond to the AP Spanish Language and Culture curriculum: public and personal identities, contemporary life, families and communities, beauties and esthetics, science and technology and world challenges. Assignments and activities connect to the AP themes and all students take practice AP exams given in class. In addition to the two AP Reading and Grammar text books, materials used include feature films, music, native speaker recordings, authentic literature and on-line newspapers. Under the teachers guidance, students will also use text and/or video chat to gain insight into the cultures of Spanish speaking countries and to communicate with native Spanish speakers around the globe. The course is offered second semester so as not to conflict with core area AP courses. It is strongly recommended that the student take the AP exam in May. Prerequisite: Spanish 4 with at least a 70 %.
courses.prerequisites: Spanish 4 with at least a 70 %.

courses.description: This interdisciplinary program combines the SS 1 study of Early World Civilizations with a chronological examination of literary classics and complements the historical context provided by a required companion course, (101) English 9 Honors Lit. and Comp. Humanities. Related papers and projects are assigned to improve organizational and logical development skills. Literature and writing assignments will address vocabulary, spelling and grammar. A major term paper is required. Earns credits in 460 SS1 World History Honors and 101 Eng. 9 Honors Lit. and Comp. Humanities. Prerequisite: Placement Committee recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Placement Committee recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: Three specific Global Citizenship courses are required for graduation (SS1, SS2, SS3)
courses.notes: Companion course paired with English 9 Humanities course (earns credits in both)

courses.description: This course is part of an interdisciplinary program which combines the SS 1 content/Early World Civilizations with a chronological approach to literature. The course is taught by a pair of teachers, one Social Studies, one Literature and Comp. Students will focus on the connections between literature and history. Earns credits in 461 SS1 World Academic and 102 Eng. 9 A Humanities.
courses.fulfills_text: Three specific Global Citizenship courses are required for graduation (SS1, SS2, SS3)
courses.notes: Companion course paired with English 9 Humanities course (earns credits in both)

courses.description: This course will emphasize reading and comprehension skills in the content area. Supplementary materials will accompany the basic text. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and MS student performance. Earns credits in 462 SS1 World Applied and 106 Eng. 9 Applied Humanities.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and MS student performance. Earns credits in 462 SS1 World Applied and 106 Eng. 9 Applied Humanities.
courses.fulfills_text: Three specific Global Citizenship courses are required for graduation (SS1, SS2, SS3)
courses.notes: Applied level; Companion course paired with English 9 Humanities course (earns credits in both)

courses.description: The study of European history since the year 1450 lays the foundation for the modern world. It introduces students to the politics, economics, and societal changes that form the world in which they live. As an alternative to the 10 th grade Honors History, this course, AP European History would have students learn the same curriculum as other 10th grades but at a more intense level. They will understand the major themes of Modern European History, analyze and interpret historical evidence and documents, and enhance their ability to express historical understanding through writing. AP European History would increase the options for academically driven students at MAUHS. For more specific course requirements visit the College Board website for the official class description. Prerequisite: SS 1 Honors and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: SS 1 Honors and teacher recommendation.

courses.description: This course explores events, people, times, and places that have had a significant impact on the history of the world and helps students understand change and continuity over time. Students will develop analytical skills through extensive use of primary and secondary sources. Prerequisite: SS 1 and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: SS 1 and teacher recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: Three specific Global Citizenship courses are required for graduation (SS1, SS2, SS3)

courses.description: This course, as described in SS 2 above, is designed for students planning to attend a two or four-year college. Prerequisite: SS 1 and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: SS 1 and teacher recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: Three specific Global Citizenship courses are required for graduation (SS1, SS2, SS3)

courses.description: This course emphasizes reading and comprehension skills while studying the time period for SS 2 World History. Supplementary materials accompany the basic text. Prerequisite: SS 1 and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: SS 1 and teacher recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: Three specific Global Citizenship courses are required for graduation (SS1, SS2, SS3)
courses.notes: Applied level

courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with the analytic skills and factual knowledge necessary to deal critically with the problems and materials in US history. The program prepares students for intermediate and advanced college courses by making demands upon them equivalent to those made by full-year introductory college courses. Students should learn to assess historical materials-their relevance to a given interpretive problem, their reliability, their importance and to weigh the evidence and interpretations presented in historical scholarship. This course develops the skills necessary to arrive at conclusions on the basis of an informed judgment and to present reasons and evidence clearly and persuasively in essay format. The textbook is supplemented by other sources, both primary and secondary. Emphasis is placed on written and oral expression using reaction papers, reviews of self-guided outside readings, seminars, debates, and simulations. Spring semester will include a more intense preparation for the AP exam. All students taking this course are expected to take the AP U.S. History exam in May. Prerequisite: SS1, SS2 Honors and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: SS1, SS2 Honors and teacher recommendation.

courses.description: This U.S. History honors course examines the history of the United States through a study of the cultural and intellectual forces that have shaped the American character. The approach is chronological. The textbook is supplemented by other sources, both primary and secondary. Emphasis is placed on the written and oral expression of ideas through research papers, book reviews, seminars, debates and video presentations. Prerequisite: SS1, SS2 and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: SS1, SS2 and teacher recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: Three specific Global Citizenship courses are required for graduation (SS1, SS2, SS3)

courses.description: This U.S. History course acquaints the student with the common experiences that bring Americans together, while also exploring the diverse experiences that make American life rich and varied. The course is a chronological approach with several important themes: growth of national unity, the diversity of population and the development of democratic institutions. Prerequisite: SS1, SS2 and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: SS1, SS2 and teacher recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: Three specific Global Citizenship courses are required for graduation (SS1, SS2, SS3)

courses.description: This course emphasizes reading and comprehension skills while studying the history of the United States. Supplementary materials accompany the basic text. Prerequisite: SS1, SS2 and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: SS1, SS2 and teacher recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: Three specific Global Citizenship courses are required for graduation (SS1, SS2, SS3)
courses.notes: Applied level

courses.description: This course is viewed as a source of civic literacy and will survey the principles, philosophies, and practices that comprise the United States system of government and law. Students are expected to apply knowledge gained in previous social studies courses to pursue deeper understanding of American government. Contemporary issues will frame conversations about the Constitution, the courts, legislative and executive branches, and federalism. In addition, a review of major political philosophies from around the world as well as famous Supreme Court cases in U.S. history will be undertaken. Emphasis is also given to the dynamics of political decision-making and the degree to which citizens participate in political processes.

This course is designed to acquaint students with the basic concepts in macro and microeconomics. Emphasis is placed on economic thought and development through the ages and today. Students will study of consumer behavior, scarcity of resources, supply and demand, elasticity, circular flow models, inflation, unemployment, the Federal Reserve System, globalization, and the emergence of developing countries.

This course is designed to familiarize students with the basic theories and concepts of psychology, the scientific study of behaviors and mental processes. Specific attention is given to the biological bases of behavior; developmental psychology; perception; states of consciousness; learning and conditioning; cognition and memory; motivation and emotion; and personality theory. Students are introduced to the teachings of Freud, Erikson, Rogers, Piaget, Pavlov, Skinner, Maslow and others. Students will apply a variety of psychological theories to various case studies and conduct hands-on research of their own design. This is a reading intensive course, designed to foster the skills needed to succeed in a collegiate setting. Prerequisite: SS1 and SS2.
courses.prerequisites: SS1 and SS2.

courses.description: This course provides a thematic study of current issues in the United States and worldwide. Issues will include the federal budget, crime and security, education, health care, immigration, poverty, terrorism, the global environment, international trade, weapons proliferation and defense. Students will experience a variety of learning activities including debates, simulations, mapping, research assignments, guest speakers and field trips. Prerequisites: SS1 and SS2.
courses.prerequisites: SS1 and SS2.

courses.description: The mission of health education is to promote healthy behaviors that will help young people acquire the knowledge and skills for a lifetime of wellness. Our curriculum is standards-based, developmentally appropriate, and based on current trends reflected from the Youth Risk Behavior Survey. Students will practice analyzing influences, accessing valid information, communication, decision making, goal setting, health-enhancing, behaviors, and advocacy, through the following content areas: Nutrition, Alcohol, Tobacco, and Other Drugs, Safety and Injury Prevention, Mental and Emotional Health, Wellness, and Healthy Relationships and Human Development.
courses.fulfills_text: Health .5 credit required

courses.description: A required semester course, usually taken by freshman. High School physical education is critical time for transition students from skill-based instruction and activity exploration to self-directed activity and fitness management. With meaningful movement experiences provide personal enjoyment and social engagement. Activities include team sports, invasion games, cooperative games, fitness, winter sports and dance.
courses.fulfills_text: Physical Education 1.5 credits required

courses.description: A required course, usually taken by sophomores, to continue the experiences furnished in Physical Education. This course explores the continuation to practice wellness of life.
courses.fulfills_text: Physical Education 1.5 credits required

courses.description: The purpose of the AP course in statistics is to introduce students to the major concepts and tools for collecting, analyzing and drawing conclusions from data. Students are exposed to four broad conceptual themes: Exploring Data, Sampling and Experimentation, anticipating Patterns using Probability and Simulation and Statistical Inference. Students are expected to take the AP Statistics exam in May . Prerequisite: Pre-Calculus.
courses.prerequisites: Pre-Calculus.

courses.description: This AP course provides students with an understanding of the concepts of college algebra, trigonometry, and additional topics that prepare students for further college-level mathematics courses. This course explores a variety of function types and their applications—polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric, and polar. Throughout the course, the mathematical practices of procedural and symbolic fluency, multiple representations, and communication and reasoning are developed. Students experience the concepts and skills related to each function type through the lenses of modeling and covariation and engage each function type through their graphical, numerical, analytical, and verbal representations.

This course presents basic concepts of plane analytical geometry and calculus. Topics include differentiation and integration of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions with emphasis on technical applications; maximum and minimum word problems; related rates; and applications of the integral to include area and volume. Prerequisite: Pre-Calculus and teacher recommendation. Acceptance through Vermont Technical College and must meet the minimum requirement of a passing grade on the assessment.
courses.prerequisites: Pre-Calculus and teacher recommendation. Acceptance through Vermont Technical College and must meet the minimum requirement of a passing grade on the assessment.
courses.notes: VSU Calculus 1; acceptance through Vermont Technical College

courses.description: This course reviews and extends analytical geometry, introduces the concept of limits which leads to the definition of the derivative, develops standard formulas for differentiation and applies these to problems of function behavior, optimization, and related rates. Anti-derivatives are introduced and applied in physics related problems and the development of the definite integral. A graphing calculator is required. Prerequisite: Pre-Calculus with a minimum grade of 80 and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Pre-Calculus with a minimum grade of 80 and teacher recommendation.

courses.description: This course is the continuation of Algebra 1, the program that students began in Middle School. Geometry introduces points, lines, planes and angles; inductive and deductive reasoning connecting to proof. This course is an in-depth study of perpendicular and parallel lines; congruence and similarity of triangles leading to applications with right triangle trigonometry presented at a rapid pace. There is an exploration of quadrilaterals and circles involving transformations, perimeter and area. Prerequisite: Completion of Algebra 1 and MAP score >245 and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Algebra 1 and MAP score >245 and teacher recommendation.

courses.description: This course primarily covers the same curriculum as Algebra 2/ Trigonometry. Most topics are covered in greater depth with more emphasis on application problems, including those with graphing calculators. Trigonometric functions are also explored in greater detail. Prerequisite: Completion of Algebra 1. Geometry or teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Algebra 1. Geometry or teacher recommendation.

courses.description: This is the first in a sequence of four courses. The focus is on algebra. Topics covered will include rational expressions, equations, inequalities, functions, polynomials, solving linear equations, system of equations and inequalities, proportional reasoning, graphing relations and functions, and right triangle trigonometry. Graphing calculators will be used to graph functions and to explore and solve application problems. Perquisite: MAP score >230
courses.prerequisites: MAP score >230

courses.description: This course reviews and enhances the algebra topics studied in Algebra 1 and Geometry. Many of the same objectives are taught using the graphing calculator, including a variety of application problems, scatter plots, modeling real-world data, regression equations and predictions. Other topics included are right triangle trigonometry, special triangles and circle geometry. Perquisite: Completion of Algebra 1; MAP score <230.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Algebra 1; MAP score <230.

courses.description: This is the second course in the college prep sequence that prepares students for college course work. Students will study topics in irrational numbers: adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing along with simplifying radical numbers. In Geometry, students will start with basic building blocks of Geometry to build their knowledge to master topics that include parallel and perpendicular lines using deductive and inductive reasoning to prove geometric theorems, area, perimeter and volume, transformations, properties of triangles, congruency and similarity, properties of both right triangles and quadrilaterals and properties of circles. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Algebra I plus MAP tests score >245. Students not in the MAU district will also be required to take the MAP tests before the semester begins.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Algebra I plus MAP tests score >245. Students not in the MAU district will also be required to take the MAP tests before the semester begins.

courses.description: This course reviews solving equations and inequalities, linear equations and their graphs, systems of linear equations and inequalities, and operations with polynomials. The course introduces the use of matrices to solve algebraic problems and also includes the study of radicals, imaginary and complex numbers, solving and graphing quadratic functions, analyzing conic sections, simplifying rational expressions, solving rational equations, and exploring trigonometric functions. Prerequisite: Completion of Algebra 1, Geometry, and Algebra 2.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Algebra 1, Geometry, and Algebra 2.

courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide A-Level students with the skills necessary to succeed in calculus and math courses in upper- level honors high school courses and courses at the college level. Particular emphasis is placed on functions, their solutions, their graphical behavior, and how functions are used to describe physical phenomena. Additionally, the topic of trigonometry as it relates to both analytical geometry and circular functions will be studied in great detail. An overview of concepts and skills applicable to introductory calculus will be included. Although similar to the Honors Pre-Calculus course, this course will proceed at a moderate pace and will not explore the extensive breadth of each topic as done in the honors course. Prerequisite: Teacher recommendation and either: Alg. 2/Trig. Honors with a passing grade; or Alg. 2/Trig. with a minimum grade of 80%. Graphing calculator strongly recommended.
courses.prerequisites: Teacher recommendation and either: Alg. 2/Trig. Honors with a passing grade; or Alg. 2/Trig. with a minimum grade of 80%. Graphing calculator strongly recommended.

courses.description: This course will focus on the use and application of statistics to help explain the world around us. Students will delve into the mathematical world of statistics including histograms, standard deviation, p-tests, line of best fit, normal curves and more. Students will apply statistics directly to sports, history, science, medicine and many other areas of study. Real world examples will be used to build a student’s mathematical base and help students’ use logical reasoning to validate statistical findings. Prerequisites: Completion of Algebra 1 and Geometry (or Algebra 2) and Teacher Recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Algebra 1 and Geometry (or Algebra 2) and Teacher Recommendation.

courses.description: This course develops and strengthens student understanding of operations of whole numbers, decimal numbers, fractions and integers. Other topics include percents, perimeter and volume, and some basic Geometry concepts. Students will solidify their understanding of basic mathematics so that they can move forward into Foundations of Algebra. Prerequisite: Teacher recommendation; MAP scores below 210.
courses.prerequisites: Teacher recommendation; MAP scores below 210.

courses.description: The goal of this course is to connect the information provided in the two previous foundation level courses and to apply it to uses outside the classroom. Topics covered are triangular ratios, geometric proportions, the simplification of roots, algebraic computation of functions, and the connection of variables to more geometric problems. Prerequisite: Map scores between 220-230.
courses.prerequisites: Map scores between 220-230.

courses.description: Review of basic math operations using whole numbers, fractions, percent & decimals applied to dealing with money. Topics include spending, earning, managing, savings, borrowing & protecting money. Students use calculators, develop organizational skills, & cooperate in group learning. Simulations & applications for each unit will help students earn concepts & apply them to everyday life. Perquisite: MAP scores between 210-220 Focus on Statistics and NQ.
courses.prerequisites: MAP scores between 210-220 Focus on Statistics and NQ.

courses.description: Biology is an exciting and rapidly growing field of study. This course will provide students with an excellent college-level introductory biology class and prepare students for the AP Examination. Due to the extensive course content and a rigorous academic curriculum, AP Biology is a full year (two-semester) course, including laboratory. Students may receive college credit and/or advanced standing for their work. Even if credit is not awarded, admissions offices recognize the rigor of AP courses on a transcript and may factor them in when determining college acceptance. All students taking this course are expected to take the AP Examination. Prerequisite: Completion of Honors Chemistry, or Chemistry and Biology, or teacher recommendation. 10 th grade students must also receive permission from AP Biology instructor.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Honors Chemistry, or Chemistry and Biology, or teacher recommendation. 10 th grade students must also receive permission from AP Biology instructor.

courses.description: AP chemistry is the equivalent of and will meet the objectives of a college general chemistry course. Topics covered include atomic theory and structure, chemical bonding, nuclear chemistry, gases, liquids, solids, solutions, reaction types, stoichiometry, equilibrium, kinetics and thermodynamics. The course also requires students to participate in laboratory experiments, which may involve extra time before and after school. Students should plan on a summer assignment prior to the start of the course in the fall and students are expected to take the Chemistry AP Exam in May. Prerequisite: Honors Algebra (or an equivalent math competency) and teacher recommendation. 10th grade students must also receive permission from AP Chemistry instructor.
courses.prerequisites: Honors Algebra (or an equivalent math competency) and teacher recommendation. 10th grade students must also receive permission from AP Chemistry instructor.

courses.description: AP Environmental Science is a hybrid course including hard science and methods in chemistry, biology, ecology, and earth systems; ethics and decision making; and law. Integrating information, writing scientifically, collaboration, and problem solving are stressed. Prerequisite: Algebra I, Biology or Teacher Recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Algebra I, Biology or Teacher Recommendation.

courses.description: AP Physics 1 is an algebra-based, introductory college-level physics course. Students cultivate their understanding of physics through inquiry-based investigations as they explore these topics: kinematics; dynamics; circular motion and gravitation; energy; momentum; simple harmonic motion; torque and rotational motion; electric charge and electric force; DC circuits; and mechanical waves and sound. This course requires that 25 percent of the instructional time will be spent in hands-on laboratory work, with an emphasis on inquiry based investigations that provide students with opportunities to demonstrate the foundational physics principles and apply the science practices. Prerequisite: Algebra 2/Trigonometry
courses.prerequisites: Algebra 2/Trigonometry

courses.description: This course is an activities-based science course that incorporates earth and space sciences, physical science, and science inquiry. There is a special emphasis on the scientific method, problem solving, mathematics, technical reading and technical writing. Recommendation will be based on grades, attendance, math and writing skills and general enthusiasm. Earth science, physical science, physical science general, or a course acceptable to the administration/science department may be accepted in place of Unified Science for transfer students. Prerequisite: A grade of 85 in A-level English, enrollment in Geometry Honors and teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: A grade of 85 in A-level English, enrollment in Geometry Honors and teacher recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: MAUHS students are expected to take Unified Science in Grade 9

courses.description: The course will involve technical writing, formal laboratory write-ups, and higher level thinking skills. Students will be expected to process, synthesize and analyze problems. The course will be taught in greater complexity and at a faster pace than 0320 Biology. Prerequisite: Teacher recommendation, and a grade of 90 or above in A-level English and Math or 85 in Honors English and Math, a 90 or better in Unified Science or 85 in Unified Science Honors.
courses.prerequisites: Teacher recommendation, and a grade of 90 or above in A-level English and Math or 85 in Honors English and Math, a 90 or better in Unified Science or 85 in Unified Science Honors.
courses.fulfills_text: MAUHS students are expected to take Biology as part of their sequence, usually during grade 10

courses.description: This course uses a mathematical approach to the study of Chemistry. It provides an in-depth study of chemical theory, laws and principals (including, but not limited to, atomic theory, kinetic theory, bond theory, stoichiometry, acids-bases-salts, organic chemistry, nuclear chemistry).         Prerequisite: Successful completion of Unified Science Honors and Geometry Honors with an 85 average, or teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Unified Science Honors and Geometry Honors with an 85 average, or teacher recommendation.

courses.description: This challenging course explores the motion of matter through space and time using applied mathematics and concepts such as force, energy, and momentum. Studying physics helps us understand nature and how our universe works. While the majority of course content is devoted to classical mechanics (kinematics, projectile motion, Newton's Law, mechanical energy, momentum, gravitation) a portion of the time is allocated to astronomy, electricity and magnetism, fluid statics and dynamics, and modern physics. Taking physics in high school is an excellent way to lay a foundation necessary for many college programs related to science, medicine, and engineering. At least 20% of the course is dedicated to laboratory experiments involving problem solving through collaboration. Recommended Background: Strong algebraic, geometric, and trigonometric skills typically gained from Algebra II/Trigonometry with at least an 80% or Pre-Calculus with at least an 80%. Alternatively, ANY student may choose to enroll in this course after a meeting with the current Honors Physics teacher. Paired with Physics class.

This course is an activities-based science program that incorporates earth and space sciences, physical science, and science inquiry. There is a special emphasis on problem solving, scientific method, mathematics and inquiry. Earth science, physical science, physical science general, or a course acceptable to the administration/science department may be accepted in place of Unified Science for transfer students. Prerequisite: Teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Teacher recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: MAUHS students are expected to take Unified Science in Grade 9

courses.description: Major areas of concentration are cell theory and structure, the diversity of plants and animals, the development of biological concepts, the interdependence of organisms and environment, biological regulation, genetic continuity and diversity of life. It is a laboratory course involving experimentation, observation and project work; recommended for college-bound students. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Unified Science or teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Unified Science or teacher recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: MAUHS students are expected to take Biology as part of their sequence, usually during grade 10

courses.description: This course is designed for students interested in the human body, major body systems, and the individual structures that comprise them, as well as comparison between human form and that of other organisms. This requires the acquisition of vocabulary pertaining to regions of the human body and its structures as well as medical terminology and general function. This course includes, but is not limited to, collaborative lab work and projects, technical reading and writing, and familiarization with common medical practices and technology. Prerequisites: Completion of Unified Science and Biology.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Unified Science and Biology.

courses.description: This course has two components. One component is Human Anatomy, the study of the structures of the major body systems. This requires the acquisition of an extensive vocabulary describing the functions and locations of basic body structures. The other component is Human Physiology. This part of the course emphasizes research and a deeper exploration of how the body works. Students are required to read and analyze current scientific literature. Laboratory activities include the dissection of a mammal and the usage of surface electrodes to measure and describe parameters such as heart rate and muscle function. This course provides a background for those interested in medical professions and for those desiring a better knowledge of the human body. Prerequisite: Successful completion of CP Biology with an 80 or above, or teacher recommendation combined with a strong student motivation.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of CP Biology with an 80 or above, or teacher recommendation combined with a strong student motivation.

courses.description: This course focuses the students’ studies on the behavior, biology, nutrition, genetics, health, breeding and management of animals. Some main focuses of the course are animal anatomy, physiology, ecology, animal health, invasive species, animal behavior, zoonotic diseases, animal husbandry, animal nutrition, conservation, etc. This course will equip students with knowledge to pursue a variety of animal-centered professions or continue their education in fields such as veterinary medicine, animal husbandry, conservation management, and more. Prerequisite: Biology, Unified Science is recommended.
courses.prerequisites: Biology, Unified Science is recommended.

courses.description: This course uses the scientific method to explore topics in geology, hydrology, meteorology, and astronomy. The course focuses on earth-shaping processes, atmospheric dynamics, and earth’s place in the solar system. It is designed to develop an awareness and appreciation for these geosystems and their important interrelationships. Emphasis is on the interpretation of maps, charts, and tables; the use of technology to collect and analyze information; and science inquiry and problem solving skills. Students are required to do a final research project. Prerequisite: Must have successfully completed Unified Science and Biology.
courses.prerequisites: Must have successfully completed Unified Science and Biology.

courses.description: This Rigorous course is intended to reach students, with an in-depth approach to the importance of environmental issues that face us today. Students will become aware of what these problems are, the causes and the total ramifications in solving them. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Chemistry with a minimum grade of 75.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Chemistry with a minimum grade of 75.

courses.description: This course involves the study of basic chemical theory, laws, principles, atomic theory, kinetic theory, bond theory, etc. Concepts are investigated from a theoretical as well as a practical point of view. Problem solving is taught through chemical reactions and gas laws. Knowledge is also gained through laboratory experimentation, which is an integral part of the course. Additional topics are at the discretion of the instructor. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Biology and Geometry or teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Biology and Geometry or teacher recommendation.

courses.description: This course is for students to continue their study of the processes in the world around them. Topics include matter, motion, forces, energy, chemistry and, as time permits, weather, geology, and astronomy.

This course includes the topics studied in the Honors Physics section but provides a less detailed examination. Laboratory work is emphasized. A solid foundation in algebra and trigonometry is necessary for success in this course. Prerequisite: Successful completion of either Algebra 2/Trig Honors or Algebra 2/Trig A level. Paired with Physics Honors.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of either Algebra 2/Trig Honors or Algebra 2/Trig A level. Paired with Physics Honors.

courses.description: This course is a general survey of earth and space sciences, physical science, and science inquiry. There is a special emphasis on problem solving and scientific method, with some mathematics and writing. This course will cover the material in a less-detailed manner than Unified Science with the focus on practical application of science concepts. Prerequisite: Teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Teacher recommendation.
courses.fulfills_text: MAUHS students are expected to take Unified Science in Grade 9
courses.notes: General level

courses.description: In this course the major emphasis is on various organisms, the human body, the structure and function of selected plants and animals, and of local ecosystems. The course is designed for those students not requiring an intensive Biology course. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Unified Science General.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Unified Science General.
courses.fulfills_text: MAUHS students are expected to take Biology as part of their sequence, usually during grade 10
courses.notes: General level

courses.description: This course will use the scientific method to study topics in geology, meteorology, hydrology, and astronomy. The course is designed with special attention to students who need reading and/ or writing assistance. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Unified Science General and Biology General or teacher recommendation.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Unified Science General and Biology General or teacher recommendation.
courses.notes: General level

courses.description: This course introduces the student to computer programming using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Students will use simple HTML and CSS to create a framework for holding their JavaScript programs. This class will focus on game development after a brief introduction to HTML and CSS. Students will learn to build some basic games including tic tac toe, snake, and a catch me game. Pre-requisite: The course is code based so students should be able to read and problem solve independently. They should have passed English and Math on the “B” level with a grade of 80 or better or have permission of instructor. Fulfills technology requirement.
courses.prerequisites: The course is code based so students should be able to read and problem solve independently. They should have passed English and Math on the “B” level with a grade of 80 or better or have permission of instructor. Fulfills technology requirement.
courses.fulfills_text: Fulfills technology requirement.

courses.description: In this course students will further their interest in technology. Students of today will learn to become tomorrow’s problem solvers. Students learn this by using state-of-the-art 3DCAD printers and laser engravers. Prerequisite: Successful completion of Algebra 1 or teacher approval.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Algebra 1 or teacher approval.

courses.description: Students who choose to take college courses while attending MAUHS can request that the college course be approved for high school credit. Courses can be approved for either elective credit, or when pre-approved can be used to substitute for a MAUHS required course. It is recommended that college courses be taken for elective credit rather than to fulfill a graduation requirement. Note: Course-related costs such as books, tuition, and transportation are the responsibility of the student. All local colleges have programs available for high school students. See your school counselor to discuss specific opportunities. Prerequisite: Completion of MAUHS and individual college application process.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of MAUHS and individual college application process.
courses.fulfills_text: Courses can be approved for either elective credit, or when pre-approved can be used to substitute for a MAUHS required course
courses.notes: program; college course appears on schedule as 9080 College Course. Credit guideline for college courses is on p. 13

courses.description: This course is for students who are non-English speakers or for those who are still gaining proficiency in English (non-native speakers). The course is designed to develop skills in listening, speaking, reading and writing in the English language. Students will also be learning about holidays, survival, acclimation, and general practical skills for living in the United States and the local community. Peer and college tutors will be assigned (as available) to students to assist in individual instruction. Intermediate students will develop grammar and vocabulary skills by reading and studying literature and writing for different purposes. Prerequisite: ESL teacher approval.
courses.prerequisites: ESL teacher approval.

courses.description: Community Based Learning (CBL) allows MAUHS students to engage in learning experiences in a community based setting. Students will be afforded opportunities to access community partners and resources as a means to broaden their education beyond the traditional classroom environment. CBL experiences will fall into one of three categories: Work-Based Learning, Service-Based Learning, or Community-Based Field Study. Assignments will be posted and completed on the CBL google classroom. Work-Based Learning- Students will gain valued job skills and learn about a specific field or career as they participate in job shadowing or internships with professionals in the workplace. Service-Based Learning- Students will engage in volunteer work that focuses on service for the betterment of our community. Community-Based Field Study- Students will explore a topic of personal interest and work with the CBL coordinator and community partners to design a learning experience uniquely tailored to meet their needs. Participation in Community Based Learning is limited to 2 semesters per student. Approval from the CBL coordinator is required after the completion of 1 semester and enrollment is capped at 55 students each semester.
courses.notes: program

courses.description: This course is all about you and your rights and responsibilities as a citizen! Should the government be able to tell you what to do? Are people treated fairly? Should Bennington and Vermont have more job opportunities? How can people make our economy more-healthy and have a say in the laws that control our daily lives? In Civics students will enjoy hands on learning, debating the issues, meeting people in the community, and getting to know the ways that people make the difference. This is an important course to prepare you for your future after graduation.
courses.fulfills_text: Civics / Financial Literacy 1 credit required, Class of 2029 (beginning with 2029 graduates)

courses.description: This course covers all of the essential personal finance topics necessary to become a financially capable student. Topics include behavioral economics, banking, credit, budgeting, investing, career, insurance, taxes, and more. By the end of this course, students will have a thorough understanding of personal finance topics and be prepared to handle the financial responsibilities that exist after graduation.
courses.fulfills_text: Civics / Financial Literacy 1 credit required, Class of 2029 (beginning with 2029 graduates)

courses.description: This course is designed for students interested in archaeology ( a branch of anthropology, the study of humankind) and archaeologists (scientists who study present and past societies by studying the artifacts left by humans over time.) Students will look at a variety of cultures, and will be expected to prepare questions to ask and answer during class discussions. Students will watch videos, research topics via the internet, prepare projects of various types, play archaeology games, write short essays and discuss how humans went about their lives in ancient times. Students are expected to take an active role in preparing topics for class discussion and engage on both small group and full class activities.

This course will cover everything from finding constellations and planets in the sky to exploring quasars and black holes. The universe is a big place, so fun and interesting topics will not be in short supply. This course will include some demonstrations, labs and hands-on exercises.

The study of bioethics incorporates questions and opinions that are involved in medicine, law, technology, biology, and public policy. This course will examine the various views that are relevant to modern medicine, genetic engineering, scientific testing, cloning, organ donation, reproductive technologies, and the emergence of biotechnology. It will examine decisions that are made and that will need to be made in the near and distant future. Students will explore hypothetical and actual cases from a variety of viewpoints and examine the ethical controversies that arise. Prerequisite: Completion of Biology.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of Biology.

courses.description: During this course students read one biography or autobiography, one book that is considered a classic novel, and one book of the student’s choice-for example, fantasy, romance, sports, or science fiction.

Introduction to the principles of hand lettering, featuring Chancery Cursive, an Italic hand and an introduction to Versal letters. The objective is to improve personal handwriting, spatial skills and historical awareness. A calligraphy pen set is required.

This introductory course in Ceramics will emphasize basic hand-building and wheel-throwing skills. Students will gain knowledge of various methods for designing and creating functional and sculptural objects. In addition students will learn basic glazing techniques and studio processes. This course fulfills half an art credit. (This does not fulfill prerequisite for taking Ceramics II)
courses.fulfills_text: This course fulfills half an art credit.

courses.description: This course is available to students who have an interest in learning the game of Chess or improving their level of play. Students will learn basic strategies and have the opportunity to play one another as an opponent. An in-class tournament is held.

This course gives students a review of basic competencies in computer use including basic computer technology, keyboarding, Office Suite: Word Processing & Spreadsheets, File Organization, Transferring files, Basic HTML and CSS to build a website, Building games using the Block Programming Language Scratch.
In this course students will create various homemade crafts and learn strategies for board games and electronic games.

In this course students will explore the art of writing creatively by both composing and responding to a variety of writing activities. Students will be reading and analyzing the work of accomplished writers.

This course gives opportunity to reflect on the changes the world has undergone over the past several decades. This course allows students to examine the important political, social, and cultural trends of this era in history.
This semester long course develops communication and skills through reading plays, acting, role-playing, and understanding of stage techniques.

This course aims to develop safe driving attitudes and to educate future drivers in the fundamentals of proper automobile operation. The course includes rules and regulations, motor vehicle laws, alcohol and drug education, defensive driving and a limited amount of mechanical instruction. Thirty hours of classroom instruction and six hours behind the wheel are required. Extremely limited seating available; therefore classes will be offered to students on a priority list as follows: seniors, juniors and sophomores, by birth date. Students wishing to be in the class MUST PROVIDE PROOF of a LEARNERS PERMIT to be enrolled in the class. Attendance, tardies, and discipline will be reviewed by administration to determine if a student can be able to meet attendance and safety measures in the class in order to be eligible. There are individual schedule limitations, and only a certain number of students can be scheduled in the “behind-the-wheel” phase. Students cannot choose whether they register in the fall/spring semester. A 70 average in the classroom and car are required to pass. Notes: The student cannot repeat the course if he or she fails. Also, suspension or expulsion from school for a violation of the district's alcohol and substance abuse policy shall result in the student being placed at the bottom of the list of eligible students for the following year. Deadline to sign up is April 1st. Prerequisites: Must be 15 and have a Vermont learner’s permit.
courses.prerequisites: Must be 15 and have a Vermont learner’s permit.

courses.description: Students will examine the history and genres of movies, how to read them, and how they are made. By the end of the semester, students will have a better understanding of what goes on in the art of cinema. Many silent movies will be watched. True interest in movies is needed, not simply in watching them but in analyzing them.
Students will Learn to play board games such as backgammon, checkers and chess, and the logic and strategies involved in them.

Handling stress can make life feel better, not just during school but after graduation as well. In this course, we use resources that are easily available, such as yoga, breathing, peer listening, and art projects to find greater ease of mind and body. We learn how to relax, manage our time, and negotiate to get what we need. This course is designed to help each person build habits for dealing with stressful situations.

courses.description: This course will explore the archetypal texts, as well as the multi-media phenomenon. Drawing from sources such as Jane Austen, J.R. Tolkien, C.S. Lewis, Dorothy Sayers and many other notable authors, students will learn how their knowledge of various texts enhances their understanding. Through reading, writing, speaking, and listening, students will learn the significance of methodology. The course will offer literature-based instruction and provide students with an opportunity to explore fiction they enjoy. Excerpts of films will also be used to provide visual support.

This course promotes learning about the moral, political, and social implications of human behavior. Holocaust Studies will go beyond WW II to examine themes of justice, race, Genocide, stereotypes, diversity, and tolerance.

courses.description: In this course, students will learn basic elements of spoken and written language. Students will also complete cultural projects related to food, music and people.
In this course, students will learn basic elements of spoken and written language. Students will also complete cultural projects related to Italian food, music and people.

The need to speak publicly presents itself in many areas such as job/college interviews, social events & school presentations. A goal of the 21st century learning expectations is: students “speak with clarity & effectiveness”, therefore this course will provide a challenging, diverse & relevant opportunity for all students. Individual speeches should interest the student, as well as, bring new awareness to the class as a whole.

This course reviews factors that make Japan a great power with world impact. Students study aspects of Japan’s culture today and in the past. These include, food, history, religion, value systems and the arts. Some language elements are included in the course. Students develop a personal interest through in-depth projects.

This course is designed to help students gain knowledge of print and broadcast journalism and to apply journalistic style and integrity to their own stories. Students will analyze various newspapers as well as a class text. Interviewing skills will be developed. Students will write stories dealing with school and off-campus issues. Students will assess stories from their peers to develop editing skills. Legal and ethical boundaries will be explored.
Students learn basic gem-cutting techniques and become familiar with gemstones and their characteristics. Skills developed include cabochon cutting, gem drilling, and faceting.

courses.description: This course is about student rights and responsibilities in the home, school and community. There will be videos, speakers, mock trials and selected readings.

These courses address the individual math needs of students. IXL will be used to customize practice materials suited for immediate feedback on progress. Students MUST be recommended in order to enroll.

Students will explore and evaluate the ways in which news is reported and portrayed across various media in the 21st century. Students will also learn how to report the news themselves across these forms of media, which may include: Newspaper, radio, television, social media, podcasts, and blogs.

Water study includes a River Watch study, including information on the Hudson River watershed, macro and some micro organisms, water quality, geology and Roaring Branch as a laboratory. Prerequisite: Unified Science.
courses.prerequisites: Unified Science.

courses.description: This course will introduce students to a variety of contemporary music including; pop, rock, hip-hop, rap, alternative, country and more. Artists will range from Taylor Swift, Zach Bryan to Tupac and Queen. Like poetry, music has voice, tone, meaning, theme and emotion. We will write about this, as we compare and critique music with poetry techniques, from and structure.

This course is available to those students who wish to write and share their poetry. Skills include the ability to listen well, read dramatically and interpret classical as well as contemporary poetry and its cultural function. Publication is a goal.

Quick techniques and shortcuts are emphasized. Students will create a quilt for an at-risk baby and will have the opportunity to make a quilt for themselves. This course provides a fun way for students to provide a community service. Materials provided for baby quilts. This course fills .5 of required art credit.
