courses.description: Are the differences we see between people based upon biological facts or rooted in social differences? The course will consider universal tendencies of human beings in trying to explain the world. In what ways do these inclinations determine the way we think about race? Through news, media, texts, and film, students will develop a depth of understanding on this complicated topic. Assessments will focus on a written and oral presentation related to semester long research of a specific area related to the topic of race. The course is designed as an extension or compliment to Holocaust Studies, but does not require any prerequisite.

courses.description: This course will be focused on teaching students about the exciting developments in renewable energy technologies and practices. The focus is how these efforts can save people and institutions on energy bills & at the same time help heal our environment. The course will provide an introduction to & comparison of several leading options, along with actual applications of these affordable solutions.

This course is designed to provide students with the information necessary to achieve the highest possible score or college admissions tests. Students will take sample tests and learn valuable test-taking skills.
Students will explore the history of science fiction in the cinema by observing films, past and present. Some reading and writing will be included.

The overriding goal of this course is to produce a science fair project. It will require the student to inquire about an issue, research the issue, and present the findings of the research to an audience with appropriate accessories. To do this the student will have to finish the following steps. (1) Pose a scientifically researchable question; (2) find information about the subject topic; (3) do appropriate research and investigation; (4) collect and analyze the results; and (5) display the findings.

Students will gain knowledge of what it takes to be a sports journalist by learning the ins and outs of how to write for a publication: The Patriot Press. Students will be responsible for writing 2-3 stories each week and will be responsible for attending sporting events.

Students will be responsible for a more hands-on approach dealing with lay-out and incorporating photojournalism into The Patriot Press. Advanced students learn “beat” reporting and work closely with the Intro to Sports Journalism students. Students are responsible for attending sporting events.

In this course, we will introduce and explore the principles of statistical reasoning with exciting, interesting, and relevant examples in sports showing how statistics is a part of everyday life. The course will make statistics exciting with high interest sports (and life) examples that show how statistics is a part of everyday life. We will examine fascinating questions about sports and life by investigating the underlying statistical questions and creating a fun atmosphere in the classroom in which students perform simulations, analyze data, and use simple randomization processes to develop an understanding of statistics. Prerequisite is geometry.

This course covers all aspects of strength and conditioning issues. It combines two days of classroom lecture and discussion, with 3 days of activity/learn-by-doing sessions. The book Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, by the National Strength and Conditioning Association, will be used to provide a science-based lecture. The activity/learn-by-doing sessions will provide training that parallels the classroom lectures. It is recommended that students taking this course be in good physical condition before taking this class. Note: This course does not take the place of PE1 or PE2. Prerequisite: PE1 and PE2
courses.prerequisites: PE1 and PE2

courses.description: This course provides an in-depth look at the conflict in Vietnam, including its impact on American society.

courses.description: This is a Social Studies civics class offering students an in-depth study of the fundamental of United States government. Students will be studying the local, state and federal governments along with a look at how the government affects the lifestyles of American citizens. Guest speakers and field trips will be included in this courses. Students work will consist of reading assignments, creating projects, opinion writing, and discussing the governmental issues of the day.

This class will introduce students to outdoor pursuits. The course will stimulate lifelong learning and recreation in the outdoors. The topic of study will include wilderness first aid, an introduction to hiking and backpacking, canoeing, mammals and tracking, fly-fishing and entomology, fire building, map and compass skills, and survival. Students will have rewarding hands-on experience in the field.
This class will introduce students to various historical films which represent significant eras in history that helped to shape our world today.

This course will teach students that they are NOT helpless, that they themselves can make positive change happen. The key to this change is to understand and celebrate the differences in people. Students will be actively engaged in learning about different ways people interact with other people and their environment. Students will also learn about world languages, life styles, religions, music, art, history and conflict resolution.

This course will focus on the many areas of yearbook production: photography, layout, copy-writing, editing and proofing. Students also will learn the business of book production, including skills such as fund-raising, advertising, communicating with parents, students, and faculty, managing a budget and organizing large amounts of material. Yearbook staff members are required to attend after school events for coverage. Students are encouraged to register for this course more than once. Prerequisite: Pending application and teacher approval. Art/Tech credit.
courses.prerequisites: Pending application and teacher approval. Art/Tech credit.

courses.description: This course is designed for students who want to explore yoga’s philosophy and physical practice. Daily yoga exercises help balance the mind and body, increase strength and flexibility, improve coordination and balance. This class teaches a non-competitive alternative to sports. Activities are intended to increase awareness of the senses and overall body awareness; help cultivate a healthy body image; reduce stress, anxiety and depression. Daily yoga practice builds emotional strength, self-esteem and self-acceptance; teaches self-love and techniques to help improve focus and attention. Activities will include breathing exercises, meditation, yoga asana practice, hot hatha yoga, synergy partner yoga, games and relaxation.

Dual Enrollment is offered to juniors and seniors. Students can earn up to six college credits. Additionally, some course credits can be applied toward high school requirements. Each student is allotted two Dual Enrollment vouchers. All courses taken at a college either online or on campus will reflect on the students’ transcript even if they failed the course.
courses.notes: program; offered to juniors and seniors; high school credit guideline: three-credit college course = 1.0 high school credit (see p. 13)

courses.description: The Early College Program allows Vermont high school seniors, who are on track to graduate, and who have participated in at least one off-campus college level course, to complete their senior year high school requirements by taking approved courses at a local Vermont approved college. According to the Vermont Agency of Education, “The Early College Program (ECP) simultaneously serves as a student's senior year of high school and a full year of college credit. Students may take a year-long course of study in any discipline.” Speak with a counselor for more information.
courses.notes: program; for Vermont high school seniors

courses.description: The VHS Collaborative offers a full catalogue of semester and full year core, honors, elective and advanced placement (AP) online courses. VHS courses engage students in global online classrooms and prepare them for college and careers in the 21st century. Courses taken in the core areas are factored in to a students’ GPA and will be calculated into the class rank. AP courses taken through VHS and MAUHS are weighted at grade earned plus 5% on the 100-point scale. If an AP course is taken, but the exam is not taken, the course will remain weighted, but the course name will change to honors. AP courses typically involved summer reading and assignments. Interested students in VHS courses should speak with their school counselor. Students must meet eligibility requirements and complete the application process.
courses.notes: program; full catalogue of semester and full-year online courses not listed individually in this catalog
